body.p: JALv3 supports native arrays with more than one dimension. Any number of dimensions may be declared; the elements are stored in row-major order in one contiguous block.
body.codeblock: VAR BYTE matrix[ROWS][COLS] VAR BYTE cube[X][Y][Z]
body.p: Access uses one subscript per dimension, and each dimension is numbered from zero. Constant and runtime subscripts may be mixed freely.
body.codeblock:
VAR BYTE matrix[4][8] VAR BYTE cube[2][3][4]
matrix[1][2] = 42 VAR BYTE value = cube[1][0][1] VAR BYTE row = 3 matrix[row][2] = value
body.p: An initializer may be written as nested lists; the inner list corresponds to the last dimension:
COUNT returns the extent of the first dimension. Applying a subscript first asks for the extent of the next dimension:
Multi-dimensional arrays can have any element type, including BIT and the wide integer types. See for the packed bit-array form.
As with one-dimensional arrays, there is no runtime bounds checking when a variable is used as a subscript. A constant subscript outside the declared range is a compile error.
